document_title: Applied Optoelectronics says power is one reason its 2027 expansion will take longer
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
The laser chips are made only in Sugar Land.

The maker is Applied Optoelectronics, headquartered there. It builds optical transceivers for internet and AI data centers. Its chief financial officer expects equipment for over 500,000 pieces of 800G and 1.6 Tb products a month by the end of 2026. Capacity for over 1 million a month is expected by the end of 2027.

The November 5th results release says the company's 2027 expansion plan in the United States will take longer. The reason given is a longer than expected wait for electrical power, among other construction issues. It does not say which building is waiting, or how much of the 2027 capacity the United States plan carries.

The slides walk a new bay taped out for machines and lit only through its dock door, drawn to illustrate.

Which site is the power for, and who is supplying it?

S1.headline: Built for light, waiting on power
S1.body: Applied Optoelectronics, a Sugar Land maker of data center optics, says its 2027 expansion plan in the United States will take longer. It cites a longer than expected wait for electrical power, among other construction issues. The bay is drawn to illustrate.

S2.headline: It makes optics for AI data centers
S2.body: The company makes optical transceivers for internet and AI data centers. Its chief executive says the company believes demand for AI-related optical technologies is accelerating. The module is drawn to illustrate.

S3.headline: Laser chips, made only in Sugar Land
S3.body: The quarterly report puts the laser design team there too. The company also leases about 209,665 square feet on Gillingham Lane in Sugar Land, used mainly for manufacturing. The plant is drawn to its stated floor area, not its shape.

S4.body: The company has leased two Houston buildings on Chimney Rock Road that are still to be built. Each property is drawn as a square of its stated floor area. It will also lease three other Houston buildings.

S5.headline: Half the floor by year end
S5.body: The company expects equipment for over 500,000 pieces of 800G and 1.6 Tb products a month by the end of 2026, and capacity for over 1 million by the end of 2027. Each pad is one equal share.

S6.headline: One stake for each month to completion
S6.body: The company entered into leases for the two Chimney Rock Road buildings on August 31st. The quarterly report anticipates substantial completion about 16 months later. The site is drawn to illustrate.

S7.headline: The wait, in its own words
S7.body: The chief financial officer, in the November 5th results release. The transformer is drawn to illustrate and stands for no named site or utility.

S8.headline: A hyperscale customer the release doesn't name
S8.body: The chief executive says the company recently secured a multi-year strategic agreement with a Tier 1 hyperscale data center customer. The hall is drawn to illustrate.

S9.headline: A 2027 target, a wait for power
S9.body: The same November 5th release expects capacity for over 1 million pieces of 800G and 1.6 Tb transceivers a month by the end of 2027. It says obtaining electrical power is taking longer than expected. It doesn't say how much of that capacity is in the United States.
